subject.title: [Feature]: Invoke tools directly without LLM round-trip

question: Which remaining direct-invoke surfaces should OpenClaw core support beyond the shipped HTTP/RPC/SDK and command-cron paths, and what owner/security gates are required for host filesystem, exec/session, slash-command, and CLI access?
rationale: The remaining work can expose process, filesystem, session, cron, Gateway, and node actions without a model turn, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent product boundary or security gate shape.

options.title: Keep umbrella and land narrow gated slices
options.body: Leave this issue open while reviewing the active host-filesystem and readiness PRs, requiring owner gates, safe defaults, docs, audit coverage, and live proof before merge.

options.title: Limit support to shipped paths
options.body: Declare the shipped HTTP/RPC/SDK and command-cron paths sufficient and close or reject broader host-FS, exec, slash-command, and CLI dispatch until a new sponsored proposal exists.

options.title: Approve broader direct execution
options.body: Allow broader direct tool execution only with a named security design, upgrade proof, and operator-facing controls that make the risk explicit.

recommendation.title: Keep umbrella and land narrow gated slices
recommendation.body: Leave this issue open while reviewing the active host-filesystem and readiness PRs, requiring owner gates, safe defaults, docs, audit coverage, and live proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is primarily the dangerous-tool and owner-gated Gateway security boundary where recent history points to steipete.
